title: Different types of shots and camera angles in film
author: Adobe
evidenceNote: Adobe separates distance-based shot types from focal-length cues, notes that wider focal lengths provide a larger field of view while longer focal lengths compress the scene, and describes wide and close framing as different coverage choices. This supports the taxonomy separation; it does not prove a generated image will obey a requested lens.

title: What Is depth of field in photography?
author: Adobe
evidenceNote: Adobe lists camera-subject distance as a factor in depth of field and states that moving closer changes the sharpness zone. This is supporting context for keeping distance separate from focal cue and focus target; it is not used to define a depth atom here.

title: Perspective
author: Canon
evidenceNote: Canon contrasts the stronger spatial-perspective effect associated with shorter wide-angle cues against the compressed background impression of longer telephoto cues. The page supports a visible perspective distinction, while the batch keeps all focal labels as visual cues rather than physical guarantees.

title: Batch 2 authored camera-axis and bundle mapping note
author: Teleprompter Library Curator
evidenceNote: This batch records the curator's decision to split the legacy close-wide composite into a focal atom plus a subject-distance atom, retain the legacy shorthand as a decomposable bundle, and require matched practical comparisons before lead acceptance.
